solutions.check: 28 entries verified against the grid (lengths, crossings, linked-clue mapping)

clue.text: Managed to have a few almost — a price to be paid

indicators.note: almost means not quite all of the word, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: ran a business means managed it
some is a vague small quantity

explanation.surface: Someone who got through only a few drinks finds there is a cost to pay afterwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A ransom is the sum demanded for releasing a captive, literally a price that must be handed over.

clue.text: Bug campaign transport carrying Bill? Wicked!

indicators.note: a vehicle carrying something holds it inside, so the transport wraps around the other pieces

parts.note: politicians tour the country in a campaign bus
a bill is an account, abbreviated AC
ill in the old sense of evil or wicked, as in ill deeds

explanation.surface: A cry of delight that the election bus is carrying someone called Bill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' looks like a person's name, but it is an account; 'Wicked!' looks like slang praise but is the old sense of evil.
explanation.definitionFit: A bacillus is a rod-shaped bacterium, and bug is the casual word for any germ causing illness.

clue.text: Like May's appeal to voters; "I can match that!"

definitions.meaning: Theresa May called a sudden, unexpected general election in 2017
the cry in the card game where players shout on seeing two matching cards

explanation.surface: A heckler answers Theresa May's pitch to the electorate by claiming they can offer the same.
explanation.walkthrough: Theresa May was the UK Prime Minister who called an early election in 2017; the card game is a children's game of spotting matching pairs.
explanation.definitionFit: A snap election is one called suddenly, and snap is the shout made when two identical playing cards turn up.

clue.text: Being in a good position, the Eye is going to stand on Donald's head

definitions.note: a phrase describing a state; the answer is the matching adjective

parts.note: Private Eye speaks of itself as we, so 'the Eye is going to' is we'll
to stand something somewhere is to place it there

indicators.note: the head of a name is its opening letter, so only that is kept

parts.note: the first letter of Donald

explanation.surface: Private Eye boasts it is ready to trample Donald Trump, which puts it in a strong spot.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' puts one piece above the next. The apostrophe of WE'LL vanishes in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: Well-placed describes someone or something located advantageously, ready to act or benefit.

clue.text: Crooked dodge by Trump (not Mr) — bizarre habit

indicators.note: crooked means bent out of shape, so the letters of dodge are twisted round
not says the named letters are excluded from the surname

parts.note: the two letters of Mr, an M and an R, which in the surname sit the other way round

explanation.surface: A jibe at a crooked scheme by the US president, minus his honorific.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crooked' rearranges DODGE to ODDGE, and TRUMP 'not Mr' loses its R and M to leave TUP.
explanation.definitionFit: A get-up is an outfit, and an odd one is a strange costume or habit of dress.

clue.text: see 13ac.
Boozer Eric held off, energy gone, showing capacity to act immaturely

parts.note: a boozer is British slang for a pub, i.e. an inn

indicators.note: off, in the sense of gone bad or wrong, tells us to rearrange the letters
gone says the energy letter has left the phrase

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A pub regular named Eric is held back, his energy spent, and behaves childishly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' is the anagram signal, not part of 'held off'; the E removed by 'energy gone' is one of the two in 'Eric held'. Inner child is pop-psychology for the childlike part of an adult.
explanation.definitionFit: The inner child is the playful, juvenile side of an adult, which lets them behave like a youngster.

clue.text: House annex raves about to break two May supporters?

indicators.note: to break says the rearranged letters split the supporters' letters apart from inside

parts.note: Theresa May led the Conservatives, whose supporters are called Con and Tory

indicators.note: about, in the sense of scattered around, signals the letters of raves are shuffled

explanation.surface: Someone rants about two of Theresa May's backers splitting a house extension.
explanation.walkthrough: Theresa May led Britain's Conservative Party, so 'two May supporters' are two different short names for a Conservative; 'about' jumbles the letters of 'raves' and 'to break' puts them between those two.
explanation.definitionFit: A conservatory is a glass-walled room added onto the side of a house, a kind of extension.

clue.text: Block housing — one grand crap place

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
G is short for grand, a thousand pounds
loo is British slang for a toilet

explanation.surface: A complaint about a council block of flats: a single expensive dump.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Block housing' looks like a tower of flats, but it is housing made of blocks of snow.
explanation.definitionFit: An igloo is an Inuit dwelling built from cut blocks of compacted snow, so literally a house of blocks.

clue.text: Hardly descriptive of Donald's feverishly inspired tale

indicators.note: doing something feverishly is frantic and disordered, so these letters are thrown into a new arrangement

parts.note: the two words supply all twelve letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A sneer that Donald Trump's latest story was made up in a fever of inspiration.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', joining the definition to the wordplay. The definition is satire: the setter says the word hardly fits Trump.
explanation.definitionFit: Presidential means dignified in the manner expected of a head of state, which the satirist says Trump is not.

clue.text: Put your foot in it, snapping "Trump no moderate leader, sir!"

indicators.note: snapping, as in breaking apart, tells us the letters are rearranged
no says the letter after it is missing from the surname
leader picks out the first letter of moderate

parts.note: its first letter is M

explanation.surface: Someone barks at an aide that Trump is no moderate, putting their foot in it.
explanation.walkthrough: TRUMP with 'no moderate leader' loses its M to leave TRUP, and that plus SIR is 'snapping' into a new order.
explanation.definitionFit: A stirrup is the loop a rider puts a foot into, so the cryptic instruction describes it.

clue.text: Cricketer's desire to go on stage

indicators.note: going on means being attached to the next piece, so one word is joined directly to the other

parts.note: to long for something is to desire it
a leg is one stage of a journey or race

explanation.surface: A sports star harbours an ambition to become an actor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stage' looks theatrical but is a leg of a journey. Long leg is a fielding position in cricket, deep behind the batsman on the leg side.
explanation.definitionFit: The fielder posted at long leg is called by the position's name, so a cricketer is a fair example.

clue.text: (& 6ac.) Dreaming of emails hacked with style

indicators.note: hacked, as in cut about, says the letters of emails are rearranged

parts.note: way and style both mean a manner of doing something

explanation.surface: Someone is fantasising about their emails being stylishly hacked.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across two lights, 13 and 6 Across, so the anagram fills the first and part of the second.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone miles away is lost in thought and not paying attention, i.e. in a daydream.

clue.text: Defeated Bill — was the Speaker absent?

definitions.note: describes the bill's fate; the answer is what was done to it
definitions.meaning: a parliamentary bill can be killed by speaking until its allotted time runs out
read literally: the one who talked was out of the room

explanation.walkthrough: 'the Speaker' looks like the Speaker of the House of Commons, but it is just whoever talked. Filibustering in Parliament is called talking a bill out.
explanation.definitionFit: A bill talked out is one blocked by debate running past its time; read whimsically, the person who talked went out.

clue.text: Article: 'Just southern, old, patronised women'

parts.note: the definite article
just and fair are synonyms
S is short for southern
an ex is a former, old partner

explanation.surface: A newspaper headline about women from the old South being condescended to.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Article' looks like a newspaper story but is the grammatical word the.
explanation.definitionFit: The fair sex is an old-fashioned, condescending phrase for women collectively, so it names them as patronised.

clue.text: 'Remains' rise in revolt, right?

indicators.note: a revolt overturns the established order, so these letters are overturned and rearranged

parts.note: the letters of rise, rearranged
what you are due is what you have a right to

explanation.surface: A question whether the Remain campaign is entitled to rise up against the Brexit vote.
explanation.walkthrough: Remain was the side in the UK's 2016 referendum on leaving the EU; here 'Remains' is just leftovers.
explanation.definitionFit: Residue is whatever is left over after the rest is removed, the leftover matter.

clue.text: Sleep with arsehole at end of the convalescence

parts.note: rest and sleep are synonyms
a cur is a contemptible person

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, the only one kept here

parts.note: the last letter of the

explanation.surface: A crude tale of bedding a jerk while recovering from illness.
explanation.definitionFit: A rest cure is a treatment of prolonged bed rest, a kind of convalescence prescribed for recovery.

clue.text: Finished stuffing part of bra front

indicators.note: stuffing something means filling its inside, so one piece goes into the other

parts.note: a bra has two cups
something finished is over

explanation.surface: Someone has finished padding the front of a bra.
explanation.walkthrough: 'front' looks like the front of the bra, but it is a facade hiding wrongdoing.
explanation.definitionFit: A front is a respectable facade concealing something illicit, which is just what a cover-up provides.

clue.text: President, right, is into "factual" vengeance

indicators.note: going into something means ending up inside it, so these pieces sit within the next word

parts.note: factual and real are synonyms
P is short for president
R is short for right
taken as written

explanation.surface: The President, being right-wing, is fond of 'facts' and of getting his revenge.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks around 'factual' mock Trump's disputed facts.
explanation.definitionFit: A reprisal is an act of retaliation, revenge taken against someone for a wrong done.

clue.text: (& 21dn.) Election slogan; "After numerous sand shifts, put forward legislation"

indicators.note: after places the shifted sand letters behind the word for numerous

parts.note: strong means numerous, as in an army ten thousand strong

indicators.note: shifts says the letters of sand move into a new order

parts.note: to table a bill is to put it forward for debate

explanation.surface: A political account of sand shifting before a bill is tabled.
explanation.walkthrough: STRONG for 'numerous', then 'shifts' turns SAND into ANDS, then TABLE. Strong and stable was Theresa May's much-mocked 2017 election slogan.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase was the Conservative campaign's catchword in the 2017 UK general election, so it is a slogan.

clue.text: Having big tits, needs different top (out of practice)

indicators.note: a different top means the opening letter is swapped for another one

parts.note: busty describes a woman with a large bust

explanation.surface: A crude remark about a buxom woman who needs a new top to wear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'top' looks like clothing but means the first letter of the word; any other letter would do, so crossing letters confirm it.
explanation.definitionFit: Being rusty means one's skills have deteriorated through lack of use, like metal left untended.

clue.text: Bug-like snacks

parts.note: to bug a phone is to tap it
like and as are synonyms

explanation.surface: Nibbles that look like insects.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bug' looks like an insect, but it is the listening device.
explanation.definitionFit: Tapas are small Spanish savoury dishes served as snacks with drinks.

clue.text: see 18ac.
"Sack of lolly put before one" — Brenda

indicators.note: put before means placed ahead in reading order, fixing which piece comes first

parts.note: lolly is British slang for money
I is the Roman numeral for one
Private Eye's nickname for Queen Elizabeth II, whose royal cipher is ER

explanation.surface: A quotation attributed to Brenda about a bag of money handed over to someone.
explanation.walkthrough: Brenda is Private Eye's long-running nickname for the late Queen, Elizabeth Regina, so ER.
explanation.definitionFit: To cashier someone is to dismiss them from the armed forces in disgrace, that is, to sack them.

clue.text: Jeremy's left wing sadly ain't providing transport

indicators.note: sadly suggests things gone awry, so those letters end up in a disordered arrangement

parts.note: the left-hand portion of Corbyn, surname of Labour leader Jeremy
the letters of ain't, rearranged

explanation.surface: Corbyn's left-wing followers sadly are not offering any transport policy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left wing' looks political, but it is the left end of the name Corbyn; Jeremy Corbyn led the UK Labour Party.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cortina was a popular Ford family car sold in Britain from the 1960s to the 1980s, so a means of transport.

clue.text: (& 25ac.) Conservative getting on with Corbyn at first — everything that you'd rather not be on the end of?

definitions.text: that you'd rather not be on the end of
definitions.note: a relative clause standing for the thing; the answer is a noun

parts.note: C is short for Conservative
someone getting on in years is old

indicators.note: at first points to the opening letter of the word just before

parts.note: the opening letter of Corbyn
all and everything are synonyms

explanation.surface: An elderly Tory teaming up with Corbyn is the last thing anyone wants to hear about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'end' looks like a finish, but it is the receiving end of a telephone line.
explanation.definitionFit: An unsolicited sales phone call is something nobody wants to be on the receiving end of.

clue.text: William, say, explosive sustainer of queen to be

parts.note: Prince William is an example of a royal
jelly is slang for gelignite, a blasting explosive

explanation.surface: Prince William is cast as a volatile figure who will keep the future Queen going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'queen to be' looks like Kate, William's wife, but it is a bee larva destined to become a queen.
explanation.definitionFit: Worker bees feed royal jelly to a larva to make it develop into a queen bee, so it nourishes her.
